result.summary: Extracts legacy wallet loading and migration logic into a dedicated `wallet/legacy/` directory under the `wallet::legacy_migration` namespace. It derives a new `LegacyWallet` subclass from `CWallet` to encapsulate migration-only methods, moves `LegacyDataSPKM` into its own file, and eliminates unused legacy record deletion methods.
result.problem: Legacy wallets can no longer be loaded directly, but their loading and migration code remains intertwined with active descriptor wallet classes and database loading in `CWallet`. This coupling clutters descriptor wallet development and leaves open the possibility of calling obsolete legacy methods.
evidence: PR description: 'Having this co-mingling of never-to-be-changed legacy wallet code and new descriptor wallet code makes it difficult to implement new things into the wallet.'
result.scope_notes: Large architectural refactor (+2611/-2334) primarily composed of code movements best reviewed with `--color-moved=dimmed-zebra`. Also includes minor helper extractions and dead code removal.
result.card: This PR isolates legacy wallet loading and migration code into a dedicated wallet/legacy directory and wallet::legacy_migration namespace, moving migration-only methods to a LegacyWallet subclass. Because Bitcoin Core no longer supports loading legacy wallets directly, separating this code cleans up CWallet and prevents accidental invocation of legacy routines during normal descriptor wallet operations. It is an internal refactor with no external behavior changes, building on #34909 and depending on #36823.

risk.why: A mistake during legacy wallet database loading or migration refactoring could lead to failed wallet migrations or unmigrated keys.
